content:
mira: heads-up — customer case #4578. EU app reports tail latency spikes (+200-600ms) and intermittent 401s starting ~09:10 UTC. Their traceroutes show requests landing in us-west edges, not EU. They say this started after an ISP change.

sam: can you paste a sample request id / trace id from their failing calls?

mira: trace-id: td9f3a2e. Sample headers from their client: 
```
GET /v1/completions
Host: api.redwood.ai
x-request-id: td9f3a2e
x-customer-org: org-778
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```
Response headers when routed to us-west: `x-redwood-edge: us1`, `x-auth-status: 401` intermittently, otherwise 200 but +250ms.

raj: ops-bot showed a small spike in eu-prod route mismatches at 09:08 UTC, likely DNS / resolver cache issue. Any EDNS Client Subnet info from the client side?

mira: customer ran these probes from their office: 
```
# from their resolver
dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
-> 34.120.45.12 (us1 ip)

# with EDNS client subnet
dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai +subnet=185.54.12.0/24
-> 34.120.45.12
```
They also provided a curl showing routing header: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
< x-redwood-edge: us1
```

sophie: billing note — customer saw ~4x token cost due to retries/falls to higher-latency model variant. Logging attached in the ticket.

sam: ok. two quick hypotheses: 1) our GeoIP DB on the authoritative DNS had an outdated mapping for that IP block -> wrong answers; 2) EDNS client-subnet being stripped or normalized by ISP causing authoritative resolver to return a default (us) answer which got cached.

raj: I checked our GeoIP build history — we rolled geoip v2026-03-01 to authoritative on 2026-03-05. Customer ASN 12345 was added in v2026-03-10 in the upstream DB. If the customer’s ISP started sending EDNS-subnet differently on 03-11, some intermediate resolvers could have cached the older answer.

mira: repro steps I used from a colo in FRA: 
```
# see resolver chain
dig +trace api.redwood.ai
# check EDNS client subnet behavior
dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai +subnet=185.54.12.0/24
```
Result: some resolvers (ISP cache) return us1. Cloudflare/1.1.1.1 returns eu1.

sam: can you attach the DNS dig outputs to the ticket? I'll triage TTLs. What is our authoritative TTL for api.redwood.ai?

mira: current SOA shows TTL = 300s for A records, but we had several upstream caches with cached entries showing remaining TTLs of 23k-86k (so stale due to resolver ignoring TTL or parent caching). I pasted examples in the ticket.

raj: plan:
- step 1: push a targeted GeoIP patch to authoritative that explicitly maps the customer's IP block to EU edge (will bump SOA serial).
- step 2: temporarily lower TTL to 60s for the problematic records to accelerate propagation.
- step 3: ask the customer to flush their local resolver / home gateway cache and restart devices. Provide dig commands.

sam: add: run a passive probe across common public resolvers (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, ISP resolvers) to confirm answers before/after change. I'll open INF-892 and assign to eng-infra.

ops-bot: alert: increased 401 rate on service api-prod in eu region detected at 2026-03-11T09:12:11Z (20m window).

mira: customer tried `nslookup` and still saw us-west. I asked them to run `dig +short @<their-resolver> api.redwood.ai` and paste.

sophie: note for support playbook: include quick guide for customers to check EDNS client subnet behavior and to test from mobile vs office network (often ISP CGNAT/resolver differences).

raj: I've created a short script to probe resolvers and collect edns-client-subnet behavior, running now. Will post summary in 10m.

sam: INF-892 opened. ETA for GeoIP patch + TTL change: 35m. I will coordinate with DNS infra to roll change during low-risk window.

mira: shared the commands for the customer to test post-change: 
```
# clear DNS on mac
sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
# or from linux
sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches
# or test with specific resolver
dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai
```

raj: update — script shows 6/12 ISP resolvers returning us1 for that block, 1/12 returning eu1, rest returning regional default. Looks like cached fallback path for unknown ASN -> us1. Proceeding with mapping + TTL bump.

sam: deployed authoritative changes at 09:46 UTC. Lowered TTL to 60s. Monitoring.

ops-bot: info: DNS zone update propagated to authoritative at 2026-03-11T09:46:23Z.

mira: customer confirms at 09:54 UTC that their requests now land in eu1 and latency normalized. No more 401s in the last 8 minutes.

sophie: billing — we should credit excess token usage caused by the fallback. I'll file the credit request.

sam: will keep monitors on for 2 hours. Closing INF-892 when clean.

mira: thanks everyone :thumbsup: — adding remediation steps to the playbook (explicit geoip rechecks after DB upgrades and guidance on lowering TTL pre-rollout).
